experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in a dramatic spectacle of nature. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffaloes, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views
experiences.description: Explore Amboseli National Park, home to some of Africa's largest elephant herds set against the iconic backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Guided game drives allow you to observe elephants, lions, cheetahs, and over 400 bird species in stunning savannah landscapes with breathtaking mountain scenery.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Visit the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa and home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth. Guided bush walks and game drives offer intimate wildlife encounters including chimpanzee sanctuary visits, lion tracking, and conservation education programs led by expert rangers.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Big Five Safari
experiences.description: Discover Lake Nakuru National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its spectacular flamingo flocks that paint the lake shores pink. The park also shelters endangered Rothschild giraffes, white and black rhinos, lions, and leopards within a compact and highly rewarding game viewing circuit.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Diani Beach Coastal Nature & Marine Safari
experiences.description: Unwind on the pristine white sands of Diani Beach and explore the Indian Ocean's rich marine ecosystem through snorkeling and glass-bottom boat tours. Spot dolphins, sea turtles, and vibrant coral reef fish while also visiting the nearby Shimba Hills National Reserve for forest elephant and sable antelope sightings.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Kenya
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange shared shuttle or budget matatu transfer toward Narok (approx. 5–6 hours). Enjoy the scenic drive through the Great Rift Valley escarpment.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your boutique stay in Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County. Check in, freshen up, and take a short walk around the camp to get oriented. Watch the stunning African sunset over the savannah from the lodge grounds.

meals.breakfast: Eat before landing or grab a snack at the airport — budget KES 300–500 at airport kiosks.
meals.lunch: Pack a light snack for the road or stop at a roadside café in Narok town for nyama choma (grilled meat) and ugali — budget KES 400–600.
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the boutique stay's in-house dining area. Ask for the budget set menu or local dishes like githeri or sukuma wiki with chapati — budget KES 700–1,000.

day_by_day.notes: Book your Nairobi–Narok shared shuttle in advance to save money. Carry Kenyan shillings (KES) for small roadside stops. The drive is long — bring water, snacks, and a light jacket for the highland section.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive in the Maasai Mara (depart 06:00). The golden hour light is perfect for wildlife photography. Look for lions, cheetahs, elephants, and zebras in the open savannah. Join a shared group game drive through your lodge to cut costs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to camp by 10:00 for a late breakfast. Rest during the midday heat. In the early afternoon (around 15:00), visit a nearby Maasai village (manyatta) for a cultural experience — negotiate a group entry fee of around KES 500–800 per person. Learn about Maasai traditions, see traditional huts, and watch warrior dances.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset game drive (16:00–18:30) along the Mara River area. Watch hippos and crocodiles at the riverbank. Return to camp as darkness falls and enjoy stargazing from the lodge grounds — the Mara sky is spectacular with minimal light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Full English or continental breakfast at the lodge — included or KES 500–700 if not included.
meals.lunch: Light packed lunch or lodge snack box prepared for the afternoon — KES 400–600.
meals.dinner: Communal campfire dinner at the lodge. Ask for local Kenyan staples like ugali, sukuma wiki, and beef stew — KES 800–1,200.

day_by_day.notes: Shared game drives are significantly cheaper than private ones — confirm with your lodge the night before. Wear neutral-colored clothing (khaki, olive, beige) and bring binoculars. Apply sunscreen and insect repellent before every drive.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day shared game drive starting at 06:00. Focus on the northern Mara Triangle area, known for high predator density. July is the beginning of the Great Wildebeest Migration season — look for massive herds crossing from the Serengeti. Keep eyes open for the 'Big Five': lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and rhino.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the game drive through the afternoon. Pack a picnic lunch to eat at a designated scenic spot inside the reserve — this saves time and money. Look for cheetah hunts and lion pride activity which are more common in the afternoon hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp by 18:30. Relax with a warm shower. Join fellow travelers at the lodge's communal lounge to share wildlife sightings and tips. Optional: ask the lodge staff to arrange a traditional Maasai storytelling session around the fire.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the lodge before the drive — porridge, toast, and tea/coffee — KES 400–600.
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch arranged by the lodge (request the day before) — KES 500–700.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge — try pilau rice (spiced rice dish) with chicken or vegetable curry — KES 800–1,200.

day_by_day.notes: Full-day drives offer the best value for your park entry fee. Maasai Mara park fees are approximately USD 70–80 per person per day for non-residents — confirm current rates. Carry enough water (at least 2 liters) for the full day.

day_by_day.morning: Morning nature walk around the lodge perimeter with a Maasai guide (often offered free or at low cost by boutique stays). Learn to identify local bird species — the Mara has over 450 recorded bird species including lilac-breasted rollers, secretary birds, and crowned cranes. Also learn about medicinal plants used by the Maasai.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mara River crossing point (if wildebeest herds are active) to witness one of nature's greatest spectacles. Alternatively, explore the Ol Kinyei or Olare Motorogi conservancies adjacent to the main reserve — these are less crowded and sometimes have lower entry fees. Look for wild dogs and hyena clans.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp for a rest. In the early evening, participate in a budget-friendly cooking class at the lodge — learn to make chapati, ugali, and a Kenyan tea (chai). This is often a free or very low-cost activity offered by community lodges.

meals.breakfast: Kenyan-style breakfast: mandazi (fried dough), chai tea, and fresh tropical fruit — KES 400–500.
meals.lunch: Roadside or camp lunch — beans and rice or a simple meat stew — KES 400–600.
meals.dinner: Home-cooked style dinner from the cooking class or lodge kitchen — chapati, lentil soup, and vegetables — KES 700–1,000.

day_by_day.notes: Walking safaris must always be done with a certified armed guide for safety. The conservancies bordering the Mara often have lower fees and fewer tourists — ask your lodge for recommendations. This is a great day for photography of birds and flora.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive (06:00–09:00) focusing on the Talek River area — excellent for leopard sightings in the riverine forest. After the drive, return for breakfast and spend mid-morning relaxing or journaling. Use this time to plan the second half of your trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon visit to a local Maasai market if one is scheduled nearby (markets rotate through villages on specific days — ask your lodge). Browse handmade beaded jewelry, shukas (Maasai blankets), and wooden carvings. Practice bargaining respectfully — expect to pay 30–50% of the opening price.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner experience: bring a thermos of tea or local juice and walk to a scenic elevated point near the lodge to watch the sunset. Many boutique lodges in the Mara have designated sunset viewpoints. Spend the evening stargazing and reflecting on the week's wildlife encounters.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the lodge after the morning drive — eggs, toast, fresh juice — KES 500–700.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at camp — avocado on toast or a simple salad with local tomatoes and onions — KES 300–500.
meals.dinner: Budget dinner at the lodge — nyama choma (grilled goat or beef) with kachumbari (tomato-onion salsa) and ugali — KES 900–1,300.

day_by_day.notes: Maasai markets are a great place to buy authentic souvenirs directly from artisans — your money goes directly to the community. Avoid buying wildlife products (ivory, skins, feathers) as these are illegal. Carry small denomination KES bills for market shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion: depart early for Hell's Gate National Park (approximately 3–4 hours drive from the Mara area toward Naivasha). Hell's Gate is one of Kenya's most budget-friendly parks — you can explore it on foot or by rented bicycle. Walk through dramatic gorges carved by ancient rivers and see geothermal steam vents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Hell's Gate — hike through the gorge with a local guide (KES 500–800 for a guided gorge walk). Spot zebras, giraffes, buffaloes, and baboons roaming freely alongside you. Visit the Fischer's Tower rock formation. Have a picnic lunch inside the park.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the Mara area or overnight near Lake Naivasha (budget guesthouses available for KES 2,000–3,500 per night) to break the journey. If staying near Naivasha, take a short evening walk along the lakeshore to watch hippos emerge at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge before departure — packed options if leaving before 06:30 — KES 400–600.
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch inside Hell's Gate National Park — sandwiches, fruit, and water — KES 300–500.
meals.dinner: Budget dinner at a local restaurant near Naivasha or back at the lodge — fish and chips or grilled tilapia with ugali — KES 700–1,000.

day_by_day.notes: Hell's Gate entry fee is approximately KES 1,500–2,000 for non-residents (much cheaper than the Mara). Bicycle rental inside the park costs around KES 500–800. This is one of the few Kenyan parks where you can walk and cycle freely without a vehicle — a unique and budget-friendly experience.

day_by_day.morning: If overnighting near Naivasha: take an early morning boat ride on Lake Naivasha (shared boat KES 1,500–2,000 per person for 1–2 hours). See hippos up close, African fish eagles, pelicans, and hundreds of flamingos. Visit Crescent Island Game Sanctuary by boat — you can walk among giraffes and zebras on this floating island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back toward Maasai Mara (3–4 hours). Stop at the Great Rift Valley viewpoint along the Naivasha–Narok road for panoramic photographs of the valley floor — one of Kenya's most iconic views and completely free. Arrive back at your boutique lodge by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the lodge. Treat yourself to a traditional Maasai herbal tea. Join a guided night walk (if offered by the lodge) to spot nocturnal wildlife such as bush babies, genets, and owls with a red-filtered torch.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Naivasha guesthouse or roadside café — mandazi and chai — KES 300–400.
meals.lunch: Stop for lunch at a local restaurant in Narok town on the drive back — nyama choma platter — KES 500–800.
meals.dinner: Welcome-back dinner at the boutique lodge — ask for the chef's special local dish — KES 800–1,200.

day_by_day.notes: The Rift Valley viewpoint is a must-stop for photography — arrive before midday for the clearest views. Crescent Island entry is approximately KES 1,500 per person. Confirm road conditions before driving as July rains can occasionally affect some sections.

day_by_day.morning: Dawn game drive (05:30–08:30) — the last days in the Mara are prime time to maximize wildlife sightings. Focus on the central Mara area near the Sekenani Gate. Look for lion cubs, cheetah coalitions, and large elephant herds. The July migration is typically in full swing — wildebeest river crossings are most frequent in the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: After breakfast, spend the afternoon at the lodge engaging in low-cost activities: bird watching from the lodge deck, sketching or journaling wildlife observations, or chatting with Maasai staff about their culture and traditions. Alternatively, arrange a community project visit — some lodges partner with local schools or conservation groups for free or low-cost visits.
day_by_day.evening: Final proper game drive of the trip (16:00–18:30). Request your driver-guide to focus on any species you haven't yet seen. End the drive at a scenic river bend to watch the sunset reflected on the water. Return to camp for a celebratory dinner.

meals.breakfast: Post-drive breakfast at the lodge — full cooked breakfast with fresh mango juice — KES 500–700.
meals.lunch: Light lodge lunch — vegetable soup and bread — KES 400–500.
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at the lodge — splurge slightly on a Kenyan feast: pilau, kuku wa nazi (coconut chicken), and fresh fruit dessert — KES 1,200–1,800.

day_by_day.notes: Ask your lodge about any complimentary farewell activities — many boutique lodges offer a special experience for guests on their last full day. Tip your game drive guide and lodge staff generously — tipping is an important part of the local economy (KES 500–1,000 per staff member is appropriate for budget travelers).

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the lodge grounds with a Maasai guide. Take last photographs of the savannah landscape and collect any remaining souvenirs from the lodge gift shop (proceeds often support local conservation). Pack your bags and check out of the boutique stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the journey back toward Nairobi via shared shuttle or matatu (KES 500–800 per person). Stop in Narok town for a final taste of local street food — try mutura (Kenyan sausage) or roasted maize from a street vendor. Arrive in Nairobi by mid-to-late afternoon. Check into a budget guesthouse or hostel in Nairobi (KES 1,500–3,000 per night in areas like Westlands or Karen).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Karen area of Nairobi — visit the Karen Blixen Museum (entry KES 1,200 for non-residents) for an introduction to Kenya's colonial history and the story behind 'Out of Africa.' Have dinner at a local Nairobi restaurant in the budget range.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast — enjoy it slowly before checkout — KES 400–600 or included.
meals.lunch: Street food lunch in Narok — roasted maize, mutura, or a simple café meal — KES 200–400.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local Nairobi restaurant — try Java House (popular budget-friendly chain) or a local nyama choma spot — KES 800–1,200.

day_by_day.notes: Nairobi traffic can be very heavy in the late afternoon — factor this into your travel timing. The Karen Blixen Museum closes at 18:00. Keep your valuables secure in Nairobi and use reputable taxis or Uber/Bolt rather than unmarked cabs.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Nairobi. Visit the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust Elephant Orphanage (open to the public 11:00–12:00 daily, entry KES 500 for residents / USD 10 for visitors). Watch baby elephants being fed and learn about Kenya's anti-poaching efforts. This is one of Nairobi's most beloved and budget-friendly wildlife experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Nairobi National Museum (entry KES 1,200 for non-residents) to learn about Kenya's natural history, archaeology, and diverse cultures. Alternatively, visit the Kazuri Beads factory in Karen for a free tour and fair-trade souvenir shopping. Make your way to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport with plenty of time before your departure flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Nairobi. Reflect on an incredible 10-day budget safari adventure across one of the world's greatest wildlife destinations. Carry home memories of wildebeest migrations, Maasai culture, and Kenya's breathtaking landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Nairobi guesthouse or a local café — chai and mandazi — KES 300–500.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the museum or a quick bite at a local café before heading to the airport — KES 400–700.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or pack snacks for the flight — budget KES 500–1,000 at airport food outlets.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. The Elephant Orphanage visit must be timed for the 11:00–12:00 window — plan your morning accordingly. Double-check that all wildlife souvenirs comply with CITES regulations — no animal products, ivory, or live animals. Kenya requires a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate for entry and exit.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

Spot dolphins, sea turtles, and vibrant coral reef fish while also visiting the nearby Shimba Hills National Reserve for forest elephant and sable antelope sightings.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Transfer from Nairobi/JKIA to Maasai Mara National Reserve (approx. 5–6 hour drive or 45-min charter flight). Enjoy the scenic journey through the Great Rift Valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at boutique stay in Maasai Mara. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation walk around the lodge grounds with a naturalist guide. Get briefed on safari rules, schedules, and what to expect during your stay.
day_by_day.evening: Settle in with a welcome sundowner drink on the lodge deck overlooking the savannah. Watch the golden hour light over the Mara plains and spot resident wildlife from the camp perimeter.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a quick bite at JKIA airport before departure
meals.lunch: Light snack/packed lunch provided during road transfer or at a roadside stop en route
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the boutique lodge's in-house restaurant — enjoy a set Kenyan-inspired menu with nyama choma (roasted meat), ugali, and seasonal vegetables (included or mid-range lodge pricing)

day_by_day.notes: Pack a light jacket for the evening — Maasai Mara nights can be cool (~15°C). Confirm transfer arrangements with your lodge in advance. If flying by charter, luggage is limited to 15 kg in a soft bag.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive (6:00–9:30 AM) into the Maasai Mara National Reserve — the best time to spot predators on the hunt. Look for lions, cheetahs, leopards, elephants, and buffalo. July is peak Great Migration season so wildebeest herds will already be massing near the Mara River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to lodge for brunch, then rest during the midday heat. Optional: visit a nearby Maasai village (manyatta) for a cultural interaction — learn about traditional Maasai customs, beadwork, and livestock herding (small community fee applies, typically $20–30 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset game drive (4:00–7:00 PM) focusing on the open plains. Excellent opportunity to witness predator activity at dusk. Return to camp for a stargazing session — the Mara's dark skies are spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast (tea, coffee, rusks) at 5:30 AM before game drive
meals.lunch: Full brunch/lunch at the lodge after the morning drive — buffet-style with salads, grilled meats, and Kenyan staples
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge — try Kenyan lamb stew or tilapia fillet with sukuma wiki (collard greens) and chapati

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral-colored clothing (khaki, olive, beige) for game drives. Bring binoculars, sunscreen, and a hat. July is peak Great Migration month — wildebeest river crossings can happen any day so stay alert.

day_by_day.morning: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari — dedicated full morning (6:00–11:00 AM) positioned at the Mara River crossing points. Witness the dramatic and world-famous wildebeest river crossings as millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles brave crocodile-infested waters. This is a bucket-list wildlife spectacle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Picnic lunch in the bush (arranged by lodge) near a scenic viewpoint. Afternoon game drive continuing along the river banks to observe hippo pods, crocodiles, and the aftermath of crossing activity. Look for big cats resting in the shade.
day_by_day.evening: Return to lodge by 7:00 PM. Enjoy a campfire evening with storytelling from Maasai guides about local wildlife and traditions. Optional bush dinner under the stars (check with lodge for availability at mid-range supplement).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at lodge before 6:00 AM departure
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch in the bush — sandwiches, fruit, juice boxes, and snacks
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner — three-course meal; try Kenyan beef curry or vegetable pilau with kachumbari (tomato-onion salad)

day_by_day.notes: River crossings are unpredictable — patience is key. Your guide will monitor radio communications with other drivers to locate active crossing points. Bring a camera with a zoom lens (200mm+ recommended). 30mm of rain this month means occasional afternoon showers — pack a light rain poncho.

day_by_day.morning: Optional hot air balloon safari over the Maasai Mara at sunrise (6:00–8:30 AM) — a breathtaking aerial perspective of the migration herds and savannah landscape. Book in advance ($450–500 per person; champagne bush breakfast included). Alternatively, take an early nature walk with an armed Maasai guide around the lodge perimeter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Mara Conservancies (Olare Motorogi or Naboisho) adjacent to the main reserve. These private conservancies offer exclusive game viewing with fewer vehicles and the opportunity to go off-road. Spot cheetahs and wild dogs more easily here.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner stop at a scenic hilltop with panoramic views of the Mara ecosystem. Return to lodge for a relaxed evening. Enjoy the lodge's common area lounge with a good book or local Tusker beer.

meals.breakfast: Champagne bush breakfast if ballooning, or full lodge breakfast (eggs, toast, fruit, porridge)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at lodge or packed lunch in the conservancy
meals.dinner: Dinner at lodge — grilled tilapia or chicken in coconut sauce with rice and greens; dessert of mandazi (Kenyan doughnuts) with honey

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon must be pre-booked — confirm with your lodge or travel agent. The Mara Conservancies require a separate conservancy fee (~$80–120/day) but offer superior, uncrowded game viewing. This is a great day for photography enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Check out from Maasai Mara boutique stay after breakfast. Begin road transfer toward Lake Nakuru (approx. 3–4 hours via Narok and Nakuru town). Stop at the scenic viewpoint over the Great Rift Valley escarpment for photographs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Lake Nakuru National Park. Check into a mid-range lodge near the park (pre-book: options include Sarova Lion Hill Game Lodge or similar at $150–200/night). Afternoon game drive inside Lake Nakuru National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Look for white and black rhinos, lions, leopards, and the park's famous flamingo flocks on the lake shore.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset over Lake Nakuru — the pink hue of thousands of flamingos on the alkaline lake is an unforgettable sight. Return to lodge for dinner and rest.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Maasai Mara lodge before checkout
meals.lunch: Lunch at a mid-range restaurant in Narok town en route — try nyama choma with ugali (~$8–12 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lake Nakuru lodge restaurant — buffet or à la carte; try Kenyan fish stew or roasted chicken with traditional sides

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru National Park entry fees apply (~$60/person/day for non-residents). The flamingo population varies seasonally but July typically sees good numbers. Keep windows up near baboon zones inside the park.

day_by_day.morning: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Big Five Safari — full morning game drive (6:30–11:00 AM) inside Lake Nakuru National Park. Focus on rhino tracking with your guide — both white and black rhinos are frequently spotted here. Also look for the rare Rothschild's giraffe, waterbuck, and cape buffalo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Makalia Falls inside the park — a beautiful waterfall and picnic spot. Afternoon drive along the lake's southern shore for the best flamingo and pelican viewing. The alkaline lake reflects beautifully in the afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Return to lodge by 6:30 PM. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the lodge pool or lounge area. Optional: attend a brief cultural performance by local Kikuyu or Nakuru community groups (sometimes arranged by lodges).

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before game drive; full brunch on return to lodge
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Makalia Falls — lodge-packed lunch box with sandwiches, fruit, and juice
meals.dinner: Dinner at lodge — try pilau rice with beef or chicken, served with kachumbari and avocado salad

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru is one of Kenya's best parks for rhino sightings — a great precursor to Ol Pejeta. Bring a wide-angle lens for flamingo landscape shots. The park is compact and very manageable in a day.

day_by_day.morning: Check out from Lake Nakuru lodge. Drive north to Ol Pejeta Conservancy near Nanyuki (approx. 2.5–3 hours). Check into a mid-range camp inside or adjacent to Ol Pejeta (options: Sweetwaters Serena Camp or similar at $180–220/night). Begin Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking experience — visit the Baraka Sanctuary to meet the last two northern white rhinos on Earth (Najin and Fatu) in a guided, intimate encounter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive inside Ol Pejeta Conservancy — the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa. Also home to all Big Five. Visit the chimpanzee sanctuary (Jane Goodall Institute) for a unique primate encounter not found in other Kenyan parks.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks on the conservancy plains with views of Mount Kenya's snow-capped peaks (weather permitting). Return to camp for a campfire dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Lake Nakuru lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a café in Nyahururu or Nanyuki town en route — try githeri (maize and bean stew) or a toasted sandwich ($5–10)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ol Pejeta camp — bush-style dinner with grilled meats, roasted vegetables, and local Kenyan flavors

day_by_day.notes: The northern white rhino encounter at Ol Pejeta is a deeply moving and historically significant experience — only two remain in the world. Conservancy fees are included in most camp rates. Ol Pejeta also supports community projects — consider purchasing local crafts from the conservancy shop.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive in Ol Pejeta (6:00–9:30 AM) — excellent Big Five territory with lions, elephants, leopards, buffalo, and both black and white rhinos. The conservancy's open grasslands and acacia woodland offer diverse habitats and superb wildlife density.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive south toward Amboseli (approx. 5–6 hours via Nairobi or via Namanga). Alternatively, take a domestic flight from Nanyuki airstrip to Amboseli (approx. 1 hour; ~$150–200 one way — recommended to save time). Check into a mid-range lodge near Amboseli National Park (options: Amboseli Sopa Lodge or Kibo Safari Camp at $150–200/night).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Amboseli in time for a short late-afternoon game drive or simply relax at the lodge with views of Kilimanjaro (Africa's highest peak) glowing in the sunset light — a classic Kenya moment.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Ol Pejeta camp
meals.lunch: Packed lunch en route or airport café snack if flying
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at Amboseli lodge — try Kenyan BBQ platter or pasta with local vegetables; enjoy the open-air dining experience

day_by_day.notes: Flying between Ol Pejeta and Amboseli is strongly recommended to maximize time. Book domestic flights in advance through Safarilink, AirKenya, or Fly540. Kilimanjaro is best visible in the early morning — set your alarm for sunrise views.

day_by_day.morning: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views — full morning game drive (6:00–10:30 AM) in Amboseli National Park. Home to some of Africa's largest and most relaxed elephant herds (often 50–100 individuals), offering extraordinary close-up encounters. The iconic backdrop of snow-capped Kilimanjaro (5,895m) makes this one of Africa's most photographed wildlife scenes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Observation Hill inside the park for a panoramic 360° view of Amboseli's swamps, plains, and Kilimanjaro. Afternoon game drive focusing on the swamp areas where elephants wade through papyrus reeds — a magical photographic opportunity. Also look for large herds of zebra, wildebeest, and Cape buffalo.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at the lodge with unobstructed Kilimanjaro views. The mountain turns golden-pink at dusk — a spectacular end to a perfect day. Optional: cultural visit to a local Maasai community near Amboseli for an evening dance performance.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before game drive; full brunch on return
meals.lunch: Lunch at lodge — buffet with salads, grilled proteins, and Kenyan sides
meals.dinner: Dinner at lodge — try slow-cooked Kenyan lamb or fresh tilapia from the lodge menu; finish with a local dessert like mandazi or tropical fruit salad

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli is one of the best parks in Africa for elephant photography — bring your longest lens. The dust from Amboseli's dry lake bed can be heavy in the afternoon; wear a buff or scarf. July weather should be clear with good Kilimanjaro visibility in the mornings.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise game drive in Amboseli (6:00–8:30 AM) — catch the golden morning light on Kilimanjaro with elephant silhouettes in the foreground. A perfect farewell to Kenya's wilderness. Return to lodge by 9:00 AM for a full breakfast and checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Amboseli to Nairobi (approx. 4 hours by road via Emali, or 1-hour charter flight to Wilson Airport). If time allows before departure, visit the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust elephant orphanage in Nairobi (open 11:00 AM–12:00 PM; $7 entry) or browse the Kazuri Beads factory and Maasai Market for last-minute souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) for departure flight. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day journey through some of Africa's most iconic wildlife destinations.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast before checkout — make it count!
meals.lunch: Lunch in Nairobi at a mid-range restaurant — try Carnivore Restaurant (famous Kenyan BBQ institution, $25–35/person) or a café in the Karen or Westlands neighborhood
meals.dinner: Airport dinner or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international flight departure for JKIA check-in and security. Confirm your return flight timing and plan your Amboseli departure accordingly. Keep $50 USD cash handy for any last-minute tips, park fees, or souvenirs. Kenya requires a valid e-visa — ensure it covers your full stay.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Kenya Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in a dramatic spectacle of nature. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffaloes, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views
experiences.description: Explore Amboseli National Park, home to some of Africa's largest elephant herds set against the iconic backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Guided game drives allow you to observe elephants, lions, cheetahs, and over 400 bird species in stunning savannah landscapes with breathtaking mountain scenery.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Visit the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa and home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth. Guided bush walks and game drives offer intimate wildlife encounters including chimpanzee sanctuary visits, lion tracking, and conservation education programs led by expert rangers.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Big Five Safari
experiences.description: Discover Lake Nakuru National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its spectacular flamingo flocks that paint the lake shores pink. The park also shelters endangered Rothschild giraffes, white and black rhinos, lions, and leopards within a compact and highly rewarding game viewing circuit.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Diani Beach Coastal Nature & Marine Safari
experiences.description: Unwind on the pristine white sands of Diani Beach and explore the Indian Ocean's rich marine ecosystem through snorkeling and glass-bottom boat tours. Spot dolphins, sea turtles, and vibrant coral reef fish while also visiting the nearby Shimba Hills National Reserve for forest elephant and sable antelope sightings.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Upon landing, you will be met by a private luxury transfer service with a dedicated concierge who assists with luggage and customs formalities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury road transfer from Nairobi to Maasai Mara National Reserve (approximately 5–6 hours via the scenic Rift Valley escarpment route). En route, stop at a panoramic viewpoint overlooking the Great Rift Valley for photographs and a curated charcuterie and champagne roadside picnic prepared by your lodge.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your boutique luxury lodge in the Maasai Mara as the golden hour sets over the savannah. Enjoy a warm welcome with cold towels, signature cocktails, and a private camp orientation. Settle into your suite and unwind on your private deck watching the sunset paint the Mara plains.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport lounge dining prior to arrival
meals.lunch: Curated gourmet picnic box with artisan sandwiches, charcuterie, tropical fruits, and chilled champagne at the Rift Valley scenic viewpoint
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the lodge's open-air boma under the stars — a three-course à la carte menu featuring Kenyan-inspired cuisine such as slow-braised nyama choma, saffron-spiced lentil soup, and pan-seared tilapia with coconut cream, paired with fine South African wines

day_by_day.notes: Dress in light, breathable layers for the afternoon drive. The lodge will provide a full briefing on safari schedules and safety protocols during the welcome dinner. Confirm any dietary requirements with the lodge concierge upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning full-day Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari game drive departing at 06:00 in a private 4x4 Land Cruiser with a dedicated expert Maasai guide. July is peak Great Migration season — witness vast columns of wildebeest and zebra moving across the Mara plains. Seek out dramatic river crossings at the Mara River where crocodiles and hippos await.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the afternoon game drive through the Mara Triangle, tracking lion prides, cheetahs, and elephant herds. Enjoy a gourmet bush lunch served in the shade of an acacia tree — a fully laid table set up by your lodge team with chilled beverages, grilled meats, and fresh salads.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge at dusk for sundowner cocktails on the elevated viewing deck overlooking a watering hole. Freshen up with an in-suite outdoor bush shower, then enjoy a private candlelit dinner on your suite's deck with personalized chef service.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn bush breakfast at the lodge — freshly baked pastries, tropical fruit platters, eggs cooked to order, Kenyan single-origin coffee and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Luxury bush picnic lunch in the Mara — grilled chicken skewers, quinoa salads, artisan breads, local cheeses, fresh fruit, and chilled sparkling water and wine
meals.dinner: Private candlelit deck dinner — five-course tasting menu featuring Mara-inspired dishes: wild mushroom velouté, pan-roasted guinea fowl, Kenyan-spiced lamb rack, and a passionfruit panna cotta dessert, with sommelier-selected wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Binoculars, wildlife field guides, and high-SPF sunscreen provided by the lodge. Migration river crossings are unpredictable — your guide will position you strategically for the best viewing opportunities. Wear muted earth-tone clothing to blend with the environment.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive hot-air balloon safari over the Maasai Mara at sunrise (06:00 departure). Float silently above the golden savannah watching the Great Migration herds, lion prides, and giraffes from a bird's-eye perspective as the morning light bathes the landscape. The flight lasts approximately one hour.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, enjoy a traditional champagne bush breakfast in the wilderness. Return to the lodge for a midday spa treatment — choose from a signature Maasai-inspired massage using local herbs and oils, or a rejuvenating body wrap at the lodge's luxury wellness spa.
day_by_day.evening: Guided walking safari at golden hour with an armed Maasai ranger and expert naturalist guide, exploring the ecosystem around the lodge on foot — track animal prints, learn about medicinal plants, and observe smaller wildlife up close. Return for a communal boma dinner with traditional Maasai cultural performances.

meals.breakfast: Champagne bush breakfast served in the wild after the balloon landing — smoked salmon, scrambled eggs, fresh croissants, tropical fruits, and Moët & Chandon champagne
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the lodge — grilled Nile perch tacos, avocado and mango salad, freshly squeezed juices, and a selection of Kenyan craft beers
meals.dinner: Communal boma dinner with Maasai cultural entertainment — a lavish buffet of nyama choma (roasted meats), ugali, sukuma wiki, grilled vegetables, and traditional Kenyan stews, followed by honey-spiced chai and desserts

day_by_day.notes: Hot-air balloon safaris must be pre-booked and are weather-dependent. Weight limits apply — confirm with the lodge. Walking safaris require closed-toe shoes. The boma dinner is a unique cultural experience — feel free to interact with the Maasai warriors and dancers.

day_by_day.morning: Private early morning game drive (06:00) focused on predator tracking in the Mara North Conservancy — a more exclusive, less-crowded zone adjacent to the main reserve. Your expert guide will use radio networks with other guides to locate leopard, wild dog, and cheetah sightings. The conservancy allows off-road driving for closer wildlife encounters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a traditional Maasai village (manyatta) for an authentic cultural immersion experience — meet the village elder, learn about Maasai traditions, bead-making, and cattle herding culture. Browse handcrafted Maasai jewelry and textiles directly from local artisans. Return to the lodge for a leisurely afternoon by the infinity pool.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private sundowner experience at a scenic hilltop in the conservancy — your lodge team sets up a bespoke cocktail station with premium spirits, canapés, and a personal butler. Watch the sun dip below the Mara horizon in complete privacy.

meals.breakfast: Full English-style safari breakfast at the lodge — freshly baked bread, eggs Benedict, grilled tomatoes, sautéed mushrooms, fresh fruit, and Kenyan AA coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Maasai village — traditional Kenyan meal of chapati, bean stew, and fresh vegetables prepared by village women, served in an authentic setting
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the lodge restaurant — a curated four-course menu featuring pan-seared duck breast with tamarind glaze, roasted butternut soup, Kenyan lobster thermidor, and a dark chocolate fondant with vanilla bean ice cream

day_by_day.notes: The Maasai village visit includes a small conservation contribution fee that supports the community directly. Bring small USD notes for purchasing crafts. The Mara North Conservancy requires a separate conservancy fee — typically included in luxury lodge packages.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from Maasai Mara airstrip to Amboseli National Park (approximately 45 minutes). Upon arrival, transfer to a luxury tented camp at the foot of Mount Kilimanjaro. Begin the Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views experience with an afternoon game drive — Amboseli is home to Africa's largest free-roaming elephant herds with Kilimanjaro as a dramatic backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Extended afternoon game drive through Amboseli's diverse ecosystems — papyrus swamps, open plains, and acacia woodlands. Observe massive elephant bulls, hippos in the swamps, and large flocks of flamingos on the seasonal lake. On clear July days, Kilimanjaro's snow-capped peak offers breathtaking photography opportunities.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp for a private sundowner on the viewing deck with unobstructed Kilimanjaro views. Enjoy a stargazing session with the camp's resident astronomer using high-powered telescopes — the Amboseli skies are exceptionally clear in July.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast at the Mara lodge before the flight departure — fresh pastries, yogurt, tropical fruits, and coffee
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at the Amboseli luxury camp — a light menu of grilled tilapia, garden salads, freshly baked focaccia, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at the camp's open-sided dining pavilion with Kilimanjaro silhouette views — three-course menu of roasted tomato bisque, slow-cooked Kenyan beef tenderloin with truffle jus, and a coconut and mango tart

day_by_day.notes: The private charter flight is the most efficient transfer option between the Mara and Amboseli. Confirm luggage weight limits for bush flights (typically 15kg in soft bags). July mornings in Amboseli can be cool — bring a light fleece for early drives.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Amboseli elephant research experience — join the camp's resident wildlife researcher for an exclusive behind-the-scenes look at the Amboseli Elephant Research Project, one of the world's longest-running elephant studies. Learn to identify individual elephants by ear patterns and tusk shapes. Morning game drive with a focus on elephant family dynamics and behavior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided nature walk with a Maasai guide and armed ranger through the Amboseli wetlands — explore the papyrus swamps fed by underground streams from Kilimanjaro's glaciers. Observe buffalo, warthogs, and hundreds of bird species including African fish eagles and saddle-billed storks. Afternoon game drive at golden hour for Kilimanjaro photography.
day_by_day.evening: Private in-suite dinner on your tent's veranda — a romantic candlelit setup with a personalized menu prepared by the camp's private chef, accompanied by the sounds of the African night and distant elephant calls.

meals.breakfast: Bush breakfast served in the field during the morning drive — freshly brewed coffee, boiled eggs, smoked salmon on rye, and seasonal fruits
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the Amboseli wetlands — gourmet sandwiches, cold cuts, fresh salads, homemade lemonade, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Private in-suite veranda dinner — five-course chef's tasting menu: amuse-bouche of avocado mousse, butternut and ginger soup, pan-roasted guinea fowl, Kenyan coffee-rubbed beef fillet, and a passionfruit soufflé with Chantilly cream

day_by_day.notes: The elephant research experience is exclusive and must be pre-arranged with the camp. Wear neutral colors for the wetland walk. Mosquito repellent is essential in the wetland areas — the camp provides high-quality DEET-free repellents.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from Amboseli to Ol Pejeta Conservancy in Laikipia (approximately 1 hour). Check in to a luxury conservancy lodge. Begin the Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking experience with a morning guided rhino tracking walk — accompanied by an armed ranger and expert tracker, follow the trails of the critically endangered black rhinos through the bush.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Ol Pejeta Chimpanzee Sanctuary — the only place in Kenya where you can see rescued chimpanzees in a semi-wild environment. Afternoon game drive through the conservancy searching for the Big Five, including the resident southern white rhinos and Ol Pejeta's famous lions. Visit the enclosure of the last two northern white rhinos on Earth — a profoundly moving conservation experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset game drive along the Ewaso Nyiro River — prime time for elephant and buffalo sightings at the water's edge. Return to the lodge for a conservation-themed dinner where a portion of proceeds supports Ol Pejeta's rhino protection programs.

meals.breakfast: Early departure breakfast at the Amboseli camp — packed breakfast box with croissants, hard-boiled eggs, fresh fruit, and a thermos of Kenyan coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Ol Pejeta lodge — a buffet of Kenyan and international dishes: grilled meats, vegetable curries, fresh salads, and homemade desserts
meals.dinner: Conservation dinner at the lodge — a four-course menu with a story: each dish is paired with a narrative about Kenyan conservation efforts, featuring dishes like Laikipia honey-glazed duck, wild herb-crusted lamb, and a chocolate and coffee tart

day_by_day.notes: Ol Pejeta is a private conservancy — game drives here allow off-road driving and night drives, which are not permitted in national parks. The northern white rhino visit is deeply emotional — your guide will provide full historical context. Photography is encouraged but flash is prohibited near the rhinos.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from Ol Pejeta to Lake Nakuru (approximately 45 minutes). Transfer to a luxury lodge overlooking the lake. Begin the Lake Nakuru Flamingo and Big Five Safari with a morning game drive — witness the spectacular pink carpet of thousands of lesser flamingos that line the alkaline lake shores, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive through Lake Nakuru National Park's diverse habitats — acacia woodlands, rocky escarpments, and open grasslands. Track the park's resident black and white rhinos, Rothschild's giraffes (one of the rarest giraffe subspecies), lions, and leopards often spotted in the yellow-barked acacia trees. Visit Makalia Falls for a scenic stop.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at the lodge's elevated terrace with panoramic views over Lake Nakuru and the surrounding escarpment. The evening light over the flamingo-pink lake is extraordinarily photogenic. Enjoy a gourmet dinner at the lodge's fine dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Ol Pejeta lodge before the flight — eggs your way, fresh-baked breads, tropical fruits, yogurt parfaits, and specialty Kenyan coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in Lake Nakuru National Park — chilled gazpacho, gourmet wraps, fresh fruit skewers, sparkling water, and chilled white wine served at a scenic viewpoint
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the Lake Nakuru lodge — three-course dinner featuring smoked trout rillette, pan-seared Kenyan lamb chops with rosemary jus, and a vanilla and caramel crème brûlée with shortbread

day_by_day.notes: Flamingo numbers at Lake Nakuru vary seasonally — July typically sees large concentrations. Bring a telephoto lens for flamingo photography. The park is also one of Kenya's best for rhino sightings due to its fenced perimeter. Rothschild's giraffe sightings are a highlight unique to this park.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight or luxury road transfer from Lake Nakuru to Diani Beach on the Kenyan coast (approximately 2.5 hours by air or transfer via Nairobi). Check in to a beachfront luxury resort. Begin the Diani Beach Coastal Nature and Marine Safari with a morning snorkeling excursion on the protected coral reef — explore vibrant coral gardens teeming with tropical fish, sea turtles, and rays.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private dhow sailing excursion along the Diani coastline on a traditional Swahili wooden sailing vessel — your private crew serves fresh seafood, chilled champagne, and tropical fruits as you sail past mangrove forests and pristine beaches. Dolphin and whale shark sightings are possible in July. Stop at a secluded sandbank for a private beach picnic.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset beach massage in a private beachside cabana. Dine at the resort's signature seafood restaurant with tables set directly on the white sand beach, illuminated by lanterns and torchlight.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Lake Nakuru lodge before departure — continental spread with fresh pastries, tropical fruits, cold cuts, and Kenyan tea and coffee
meals.lunch: Freshly caught seafood feast on the private dhow — grilled lobster, Swahili-spiced prawns, coconut fish curry, fresh mango salsa, and chilled Sauvignon Blanc
meals.dinner: Beachside fine dining at the resort's seafood restaurant — whole grilled Diani crayfish with herb butter, Swahili coconut fish stew, and a mango and cardamom panna cotta, with local Tusker Cider and premium wine selections

day_by_day.notes: Pack light reef-safe sunscreen and a rash guard for snorkeling — the Diani reef is a protected marine ecosystem. The dhow excursion is private and fully customizable. July is within the kaskazi monsoon transition — seas are generally calm and conditions are excellent for marine activities.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Diani Beach — enjoy a guided kayaking tour through the Diani mangrove forest with a marine naturalist, exploring this unique coastal ecosystem and spotting kingfishers, mudskippers, and fiddler crabs. Return to the resort for a farewell breakfast on the beachfront terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon at the resort — optional activities include a stand-up paddleboarding session, a visit to the Colobus Conservation Project to see rare Angolan colobus monkeys in the coastal forest, or a final spa treatment. Private luxury transfer to Ukunda Airstrip or Mombasa Moi International Airport for onward flights.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Diani — private luxury airport transfer with a dedicated concierge. If your flight departs late, enjoy a farewell cocktail at the airport lounge or a final dinner at the resort before heading to the airport. Carry curated Kenyan gifts and souvenirs selected by the resort's concierge team.

meals.breakfast: Lavish farewell breakfast on the beachfront terrace — a full spread of freshly baked croissants, smoked salmon platters, tropical fruit towers, Kenyan single-origin pour-over coffee, fresh coconut water, and eggs cooked to order
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort's beach bar — grilled fish tacos, avocado and prawn salad, fresh coconut ice cream, and a signature Diani sunset cocktail
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the resort or airport lounge depending on departure time — a curated Kenyan tasting platter of signature dishes to close the journey: nyama choma, pilau rice, kachumbari salad, and a final glass of Kenyan sparkling wine

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight times carefully and allow extra time for coastal-to-airport transfers. The Colobus Conservation Project visit is a wonderful final wildlife experience and supports local conservation. The resort's concierge can arrange curated gift hampers of Kenyan coffee, teas, and artisan crafts to take home as souvenirs.
